WOODS RUN DIGEST

Thursday edition

November 19, 2026

U.S. WEST — CALIFORNIA / NOVEMBER 17 ACQUISITION

Sierra Pacific plans to restart Burney’s biomass plant

Sierra Pacific Industries has acquired the Burney Forest Products biomass power plant assets in California and plans to refurbish the facility for a 2027 restart. The company says it will integrate the plant into its existing Burney operations and add about 20 permanent jobs once it is operating.

The plant uses sawmill residuals and low-value forest wood to generate electricity and steam for lumber drying. Its capacity is up to 30 megawatts. The announcement establishes a planned return of this wood outlet, without giving a restart month, purchase volumes or new supplier terms.

Sierra Pacific Industries: acquisition and restart plan →

By the Numbers

Latest available observations as of 2026-11-19. Dates and comparison periods vary by series; monthly figures remain unchanged between releases.

IndicatorLatestChange
U.S. on-highway dieselEIA U.S. on-highway diesel; taxes includedUS$5.94/galWeek of November 16, 2026; released November 17−US$0.19/gal
−3.1%Versus November 9: US$6.13/gal
Lumber futuresJanuary 2027 lumber futures (CME LBRF27)US$537.00/MBFNovember 18, 2026 settlementUnavailableNovember 11 January settlement not independently verified
Madison’s lumber indexMadison’s weekly lumber indexUS$444.00/MBFWeek ending November 13, 2026−US$5.00/MBF
−1.1% (calculated)Versus week ending November 6: US$449.00/MBF
Hardwood lumber PPIBLS WPU0812; 1982=100; not seasonally adjusted284.3 index pointsOctober 2026; released November 13−1.3 points
−0.4%Versus revised September 2026: 285.6
U.S. single-family housing startsCensus U.S. single-family starts; annualized estimate864,000 units (SAAR)October 2026; released November 18+33,000 units (SAAR)
+4.0%Versus revised September 2026: 831,000
Canadian dollarBank of Canada; Canadian dollars per U.S. dollarC$1.43 per US$1.00Daily average, November 18, 2026+C$0.00 per US$1.00
+0.2%Versus November 17: C$1.43 per US$1.00

Housing starts are annualized estimates, not actual monthly units, and are subject to revision. The hardwood PPI is an index, not a dollar price. Exchange rates are daily averages. MBF means thousand board feet. The October single-family starts monthly change has a published ±9.0-percentage-point 90.0% confidence interval and is not statistically significant. The named January settlement is from the contract table, which differs from continuous-series historical prices. The November 11 same-contract settlement could not be independently confirmed. Display rounding follows the approved format. Changes are calculated from unrounded observations, so rounded currency levels may look unchanged even when a small movement occurred.

Sources:
EIA U.S. on-highway diesel; taxes included
Investing.com January contract settlement
CME delivery calendar
Madison’s November 13 index
BLS hardwood lumber PPI via FRED
Census U.S. single-family starts; annualized estimate
Bank of Canada daily averages

Curtailment Watch

Kruger suspended its Brompton biomass cogeneration plant in Sherbrooke, Quebec, indefinitely on November 12, citing economic and operational constraints. Biomass Magazine’s November 18 report reproduces the company’s statement and says approximately 20 employees are affected. The suspension applies to the biomass facility; the statement does not announce a shutdown of the separate Sherbrooke tissue mill. No restart date or quantified change in wood purchases was disclosed. Company statement reproduced by Biomass Magazine · 107.7 Estrie’s reporting of the company communiqué

Wood Products & Markets

CANADA — DOMESTIC WOOD MARKETS / INDUSTRY ADVOCACY

Canadian wood groups join a push to remove housing barriers

The Forest Products Association of Canada and Canadian Wood Council have joined the Homes and Growth Coalition, which is developing proposals to get more housing built. Their November 9 announcement, posted November 10, connects domestic wood use and factory-built construction with changes to investment, taxes and fees, regulation and housing data.

The groups want building and approval rules that make Canadian manufacturing capacity easier to use. This is an industry policy agenda, with no enacted reforms or new wood orders announced.

Forest Products Association of Canada: coalition priorities →

Action Detector

CANADA — QUEBEC / COMMENTS THROUGH DECEMBER 15

Mauricie opens windthrow salvage plans to public comment

Quebec is consulting on recovery of trees blown down or damaged by summer 2026 winds in four Mauricie public-forest management units: 041-51, 042-51, 043-51 and 043-52. The proposed plan maps possible harvest areas and regeneration work where needed. Comments are open through December 15.

The interactive map also accepts comments, but will be unavailable from November 25 at 6:30 p.m. through November 29; service is expected to resume November 30. A December 3 information session requires registration by the previous day. This is a planning consultation, not an advertised harvest contract.

Quebec: plan, map, comments and session instructions →

Under the Radar

U.S. WEST — CALIFORNIA / NOVEMBER CASE STUDY

Forestry training support reaches beyond the classroom

A November Berkeley case study of California’s Resilient Careers in Forestry program identifies transportation, equipment and employer connections as important supports for trainees. The program helps rural participants with travel costs and supplies such as wildland fire boots, while partner organizations provide access to specialized training equipment.

The report counts 2,426 people enrolled in at least one program—not graduates or verified job placements. Its findings draw on 2026 interviews and communications with program leadership. The program began in 2022 and continues through May 2027; the case study is not a new funding or enrollment announcement.

Berkeley Center for Law, Energy & the Environment: case study →

Today's Featured Resource

Northeastern Forest Products Supply Chain Climate Adaptation Toolkit

This online toolkit organizes climate-adaptation options for northeastern landowners, foresters, loggers and mills. It connects operating challenges with practical actions in harvest scheduling, roads, water-quality practices, wood procurement and related areas.

Explore Northeastern Forest Products Supply Chain Climate Adaptation Toolkit →
